citations.claim: first pole_upright violation at step 15; cart has been driven to x~0.75 with high energy ~17.0 while pole exceeds limit
one step before failure pole already at -0.724 rad with cart velocity ~5.1 and rising energy, showing runaway divergence
early divergence visible by step 8: pole already swung past upright to -0.10 rad with growing energy under noisy feedback

counterfactual.change: set sensor_noise from 0.017035943934549849 to 0 with all other fields identical; noisy angle/rate feedback was driving positive-feedback overcorrection at large dt, so clean sensing removes the failure

explanation: Shrunk scenario starts near-upright (theta=0.1) but with near-max sensor noise (0.017) and near-max dt (0.02). Noisy angle/rate measurements cause the fixed state-feedback controller to apply large wrong-direction forces (15-24 N by steps 5-12), accelerating the cart (v 1.3 at step5 to 5.3 at step15) and pumping energy (1.28 to 17.0) instead of stabilizing. Pole swings from +0.1 to -0.46 by step12, -0.72 by step14, -0.868 by step15, violating pole_upright. Zeroing only sensor_noise leaves the run stable, confirming noise-driven feedback destabilization at coarse dt.
vision_note: The cart drifts steadily rightward while the pole leans progressively farther to the left. By step 15 the pole is tilted sharply off vertical and turns red to mark the violation.
